articles.title: Selling to Spain and Italy Customers: A Website Checklist for Builders
articles.excerpt: If you build websites for clients who sell into Europe, this checklist is for you. Buyers in Spain and Italy are careful online shoppers. They may love a product or service, but they will not enquire…
articles.body: If you build websites for clients who sell into Europe, this checklist is for you. Buyers in Spain and Italy are careful online shoppers. They may love a product or service, but they will not enquire until the website answers a few basic questions. Who are you, can you be trusted, how does delivery or onboarding work, and what happens if something goes wrong. A website built only for a home market often leaves these questions unanswered. Here is what to get right, in the order that matters. Key takeaways Trust signals matter as much as design for European buyers. Clear language options reduce doubt and abandoned enquiries. Delivery, returns, and support details must be easy to find. Local payment and contact options increase confidence.

articles.title: What is User-centred Design? Principles, Process & Where to Begin
articles.excerpt: Today digital products must be easy to use, accessible, reliable and solve users’ problems in order to truly be useful. This is where user-centred design comes in. Its a design approach that focuses o…
articles.body: Today digital products must be easy to use, accessible, reliable and solve users’ problems in order to truly be useful. This is where user-centred design comes in. Its a design approach that focuses on users needs, expectations, behaviours and experiences. Whether you’re designing a website for your business, mobile app, SaaS or even Web3 product, knowing about user-centred design can help improve your digital products to provide better user experiences. What is User-centred Design? User-centred design focuses on putting your users at the heart of your design decisions. Rather than purely designing based on assumptions, you’ll carry out research to understand how your users are interacting with technology, what issues they face and what you can do to help.

articles.title: Recharge Merchants: Half Your "Churn" Never Met Your Product
articles.excerpt: Ask a Recharge merchant why subscribers leave and you will hear product answers: the box got repetitive, the price crept up, a competitor launched. Those answers describe the subscribers who decided.…
articles.body: Ask a Recharge merchant why subscribers leave and you will hear product answers: the box got repetitive, the price crept up, a competitor launched. Those answers describe the subscribers who decided. But in most Recharge stores of any age, a second population leaves each month having decided nothing: their renewals failed, the standard retry sequence ran its course, and the subscription ended by rule rather than by choice. Post-mortems rarely meet these customers, because exit surveys survey the exiters who clicked something. The silent population just stops — and the store's churn conversation proceeds as if the product had been judged, when a large slice of it was never even reached.

articles.body: If your app uses Firebase or AdMob, you have to declare the data those SDKs collect in Play Console's Data safety form, even though your own code never touches it. Google publishes a disclosure page for each SDK, and the form should match what those pages say plus whatever your own app collects. This guide summarises those pages for the most common SDKs as of November 2026. SDK versions change what they collect, so treat it as a starting point and check the pages for the versions you actually ship. The form is in Play Console under App content, Data safety.

articles.title: What Hybrid Search Looks Like When It Has to Run on Your Laptop
articles.excerpt: Suppose you are working in a codebase you did not write, and you type the following question: Where is ERR_CONN_RESET handled? The answer exists. One file contains a catch block that checks for exactl…
articles.body: Suppose you are working in a codebase you did not write, and you type the following question: Where is ERR_CONN_RESET handled? The answer exists. One file contains a catch block that checks for exactly that constant and retries the request. A purely semantic search may not put that file first. It may return a connection-pool module, a general error-handling utility and a retry helper. All three are about the right topic. None of them necessarily contains the string you asked for. Now consider a second question: How do we stop a user from logging in too many times? The relevant function is called throttleAuthAttempts . Its body talks about a counter and a lockout window. It never uses the words "logging in" or "too many times". A keyword search may miss it.

articles.title: What's New in RubyGems/Bundler 4.1, Part 2: Defenses Against Supply Chain Attacks
articles.excerpt: I'm Hiroshi Shibata (hsbt), a Ruby committer and the lead maintainer of RubyGems and Bundler. RubyGems and Bundler 4.1.0.beta3 shipped on October 28, 2026. This is Part 2 of a three-part series on wha…
articles.body: I'm Hiroshi Shibata (hsbt), a Ruby committer and the lead maintainer of RubyGems and Bundler. TL;DR RubyGems and Bundler 4.1.0.beta3 shipped on October 28, 2026. This is Part 2 of a three-part series on what's new in 4.1. Part 1 covered override and prune . This part covers defenses against supply chain attacks, in the order a developer meets them, from fetching and installing gems to publishing your own. Cooldown keeps freshly published versions out of resolution, two install options stop code from running at install time, a credential store moves your API keys into the OS keychain, and gem push attaches an attestation by itself on GitHub Actions. At the end there is a short note on the ML-DSA signature standard. Everything here is opt-in or leaves the default behavior alone.

articles.body: When the conversation turns to Tim Burton ’s best movies , the same titles tend to surface: Beetlejuice , his Batman movies , Edward Scissorhands , Ed Wood , and Pee-Wee’s Big Adventure . Even The Nightmare Before Christmas usually gets a mention, despite being directed by Henry Selick . Less likely to enter the discussion is Big Fish , Burton’s 2003 fantasy about a father whose life sounds too extraordinary to believe. That’s a shame, because it’s some of his very best work. You probably wouldn’t be surprised to know that a principle called Laver’s Law describes the cyclicity in fashion. Styles that were trendy two decades ago suddenly emerge again, while what was hip almost a decade ago becomes distasteful. Something similar is happening with accessories and gadgets, especially when it comes to music, as we witness a resurgence of retro tech and equipment.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.excerpt: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

articles.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
articles.excerpt: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.body: Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

articles.title: Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview)
articles.excerpt: "Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment."
articles.body: Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.

articles.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
articles.excerpt: Blue Origin has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the launcher even more flexible and capable. The company has also built a new engine, called Northstar.
articles.body: Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment.
